Attached is a focused spreadsheet with questions about audit chronology, preservation, exportability, and tamper evidence for audit trails (file: Aurora_RFP_AuditQuestions_v3.xlsx). All —

Draft technical notes below (high-level summary; will expand into the spreadsheet):

1) Retention windows by record class
- Control plane audit logs (API calls, admin actions): configurable retention; default 90 days hot, 3 years cold (compressible).
- Customer request/ingest logs (user prompts, request metadata): default 30 days; long-term retention up to 7 years via archival add-on.
- System telemetry (node metrics): 90 days unless bespoke SLA.

2) Export formats and packaging
- Exports produced as NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) or Parquet (columnar) with optional gzip compression.
- Each export is accompanied by: manifest.json (schema + file list), md5/sha256 checksums for each file, and a signed manifest signature (Ed25519) for integrity.
- Delivery options: S3 bucket push (customer-provisioned bucket, server-side encryption AES256 or AWS KMS), pre-signed HTTPS URLs, or secure SCP for on-prem partners.

3) Tamper evidence & non-repudiation
- Write-once append-only storage for audit streams (WORM-like semantics) with object versioning and write-guards.
- Each exported bundle includes a signed manifest; manifests are timestamped against our internal monotonic time service and optionally timestamped via an external timestamping authority (if required by contract).
- Chain-of-custody metadata captured: exporter user/service, export job id, start/end timestamps, checksums, destination URI, and retention policy applied.

4) Snapshotting and extraction cadence
- On-demand exports: initiated via API/Console, generating a job ID and progress events.
- Scheduled snapshots: daily/weekly/monthly retention tier snapshots available.

5) Access controls and auditability
- RBAC on export operations; MFA and scoped service roles required for exports.
- Exports are recorded in a separate export-audit stream retained independently for 7 years.

I'll convert these notes into the spreadsheet answers and include example manifest and checksum snippets. Ben

Hi James —

Thanks for the patience; attached is our consolidated response to the Aurora audit chronology and handback questions. Included:
- Redwood_Audit_Chronology_Response_20261209.pdf (narrative + sample manifest)
- Aurora_RFP_Audit_Questions_Answered_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with cell-level answers)
- chain_of_custody_playbook.pdf (compliance runbook excerpt)

Executive summary highlights:
- Export formats: NDJSON or Parquet (gzip optional); manifests include SHA256 and Ed25519-signed statement.
- Retention: default operational retention tiers (30/90/90 days) with archival options to 7 years; we support contractual retention windows.
- Non-repudiation: signed manifests + timestamp attestation and separate export-audit stream retained independently.
- Delivery: customer-provisioned S3, pre-signed HTTPS, or secure transfer; we provide checksums and a signed manifest for verification.

Proposed next step: 30-minute walkthrough to review an example manifest and the export job lifecycle. Are you available Tue 12/14 or Wed 12/15 (09:00–12:00 PT)?

If helpful I can also produce a short sample export (redacted) showing the manifest and checksum verification steps.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
